name: Cayenne Cheese Straws
description: Historical recipe from The Canadian Family Cook Book (1914). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

instructions.text: Mix into a paste with the yolk of an egg.

Roll out to the thickness of a silver quarter, about four or five inches long; cut into strips about a third of an inch wide, twist them as you would a paper spill, and lay them on a baking-sheet slightly floured.
Bake in a moderate oven until crisp, but they must not be the least brown.
If put away in a tin, these cheese straws will keep a long time.
Serve cold, piled tastefully on a glass dish. You can make the straws of remnants of puff-pastry, rolling in the grated cheese.

source.author: Grace E. Denison
source.originalInstructions:
1. Mix into a paste with the yolk of an egg.
2. Roll out to the thickness of a silver quarter, about four or five inches long; cut into strips about a third of an inch wide, twist them as you would a paper spill, and lay them on a baking-sheet slightly floured.
3. Bake in a moderate oven until crisp, but they must not be the least brown.
4. If put away in a tin, these cheese straws will keep a long time.
5. Serve cold, piled tastefully on a glass dish. You can make the straws of remnants of puff-pastry, rolling in the grated cheese.
